---
title: "The error–disclosure frontier"
subtitle: "2.10 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 22, and Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), slides 58–60"
description: "The lower convex boundary of expected wrong counts at different levels of disclosure."
---

Plotting every grade report by stated pairs $N$ and expected wrong directions $E$ reveals a lower convex frontier $H(m)$. Raising a supporting line of slope $\tau$ from below identifies the minimum-risk report at each withholding cost.

```{=html}
<div id="app" class="prx-app column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/frontier.js"></script>
<script>window.__prxApp = PRX["frontier"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("app"));</script>
```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **τ .20, all reports.** The touched vertex states 14 pairs with .358 expected wrong directions and risk .0372.
- **τ .15, all reports.** A lower withholding cost selects 13 stated pairs, .169 expected wrong directions, and risk .0313.
- **τ .40, all reports.** Costlier withholding reaches the strict order: 15 stated pairs, .719 expected wrong directions, and risk .0480.
- **τ .20, at most 3 grades.** Among 603 capped reports, the boundary ends at 12 stated pairs with .0248 expected wrong directions and risk .0417.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Dashed segments represent random mixtures of complete reports rather than a single deterministic card. Sites are fictional tutorial data under one supplied posterior (compare Kline, Rose and Walters 2024, Section V.E, Figure 6).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
p <- postrank_frontier(pr_tutorial$one, weights=c(score_A=1), tau=c(.15,.20,.40), G_max=6L, backend="highs")
p$table[, c("tau", "N", "primary_risk", "status")]
```

HiGHS solves each requested τ; the browser enumerates the six-site family to trace $H(m)$.
:::

Standalone: [embed/frontier.html](../../embed/frontier.html), for example `?tau=.15&family=all&view=near`.
